learn.title: Digital Defense Curriculum
learn.subtitle: Learn 4 practical steps to keep your account security and family privacy safe.
learn.allCompleted: Congratulations! You have completed all core curriculum modules.

module1.title: Password Security & 2FA
module1.description: Why passphrases beat complex short passwords against brute-force attacks, and why 2FA is essential.
module1.takeaway1: Use a 4-5 word passphrase that is easy to visualize but mathematically impossible to guess.
module1.takeaway2: Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA/MFA) on your gaming and email accounts as a second defense shield.
module1.takeaway3: Never reuse passwords across different apps; use a secure password manager.
module1.caseStudy: Dimas' gaming account was compromised because he used 'dimas123', the same password from a leaked forum. After enabling 2FA and switching to a passphrase, his account was fully protected.

module2.title: Phishing & Social Engineering
module2.description: Recognizing emotional manipulation tactics that exploit panic, curiosity, or fake prize promises.
module2.takeaway1: If a message promises free prizes but asks for login credentials or fees, it is definitely phishing.
module2.takeaway2: Inspect URLs carefully: scammers use typosquatting domain tricks like 'steancommunity' instead of 'steamcommunity'.
module2.takeaway3: Official services never ask for your password or OTP code over chat or phone.
module2.caseStudy: Sarah received an SMS claiming she won $5,000 and must click a link within 10 minutes. She spotted the suspicious .xyz domain and blocked the sender immediately.

module3.title: Data Privacy & Digital Footprint
module3.description: Protecting personal identity data and understanding that what goes online stays online forever.
module3.takeaway1: Avoid sharing school uniforms with badges, concert tickets with barcodes, or home locations.
module3.takeaway2: Audit phone app permissions: deny location, contacts, or mic access to apps that don't need them.
module3.takeaway3: Your digital footprint is permanent; always think about the future impact before posting.
module3.caseStudy: A photo filter app requested contacts and GPS location. Budi denied the permission since image filters only need photo access.

module4.title: Anti-Cyberbullying & Ethics
module4.description: Cultivating an empathetic digital environment, respecting privacy boundaries, and actionable steps to handle online harassment.
module4.takeaway1: Follow the 4 Defense Steps: Screenshot Evidence -> Don't Retaliate -> Block Bully -> Report to a Trusted Adult.
module4.takeaway2: Don't be a passive bystander; reach out in private to support friends being targeted in group chats.
module4.takeaway3: Creating edited memes of friends without consent violates privacy boundaries and is digital bullying.
module4.caseStudy: When a classmate was mocked in a chat group, Rina didn't join in. She captured screenshot evidence, comforted her friend privately, and reported the incident to the school counselor.

guide.title: Family & Classroom Guide
guide.subtitle: Practical guide for parents and teachers to support children online safely.
guide.parentsTitle: Fostering Open Conversations About Digital Safety at Home
guide.parentsDesc: Rather than confiscating devices and creating defensive barriers, build shared digital agreements through supportive conversations.

parentTips.tip1Desc: If a child accidentally clicks a suspicious link, appreciate their honesty in coming forward instead of punishing them.
parentTips.tip2Desc: Designate screen-free zones (such as dinner tables and bedrooms at night) respected by everyone in the household.
parentTips.tip3Title: Understand Your Child's Gaming & Social Circle
parentTips.tip3Desc: Spend 15 minutes playing games together to understand chat features, microtransactions, and in-game friend requests.

guide.educatorsTitle: Cyber Literacy Classroom Lesson Plan (45 Minutes)
guide.educatorsDesc: A structured lesson framework for Informatics subjects or School Counseling sessions.
guide.parentCtaTitle: Try Socratic Discussions with Your Child
guide.parentCtaDesc: Open the Socratic chat space to dissect digital scenarios your child encounters at school or in games.
guide.eduCtaTitle: Open Threat Inspector for Classroom Projector Demos
guide.eduCtaDesc: Use visual detector preset case studies to trigger active discussions among students.

eduSteps.step1Title: Minutes 00-10: Visual Hook with Threat Detector
eduSteps.step1Desc: Display sample phishing screenshots on the classroom projector. Ask students to spot clues before revealing the answers.
eduSteps.step2Title: Minutes 10-25: Socratic Guided Inquiry with tami
eduSteps.step2Desc: Guide students to consult tami on the chat room to test their reasoning on realistic case scenarios.
eduSteps.step3Desc: Students test phishing email audits and password entropy calculations in the Practice Lab independently.
eduSteps.step4Desc: Conclude the session by formulating 3 digital safety rules agreed upon by the entire class.
